reading.title: Living on Mars
reading.subtitle: Will humans become a multi-planet species?

paragraphs.label: A.
paragraphs.text: In the next few decades, humans are going to travel to Mars. NASA and private companies like SpaceX are planning to establish a permanent colony on the Red Planet. By 2050, astronauts will have built the first Martian base. But living on Mars will be incredibly difficult.

paragraphs.label: B.
paragraphs.text: First, the journey itself is a hazard. It takes about seven months to get there. Astronauts will have to survive in a tiny spaceship for a long time. They might feel isolated and lonely. When they arrive, they must adapt to a planet with almost no oxygen and freezing temperatures. They will have to wear special suits whenever they go outside.

paragraphs.label: C.
paragraphs.text: To survive, humans will need to grow their own food. Scientists have already discovered that some plants can grow in Martian soil. Colonists should also build underground homes to hide from dangerous radiation. It will be a very hard life, but it is an exciting challenge for the future of humanity.

paragraphs.label: D.
paragraphs.text: Everyday life on Mars will also be very different. A day on Mars is 37 minutes longer than a day on Earth, and a year lasts 687 Earth days. Messages from Earth will take up to 20 minutes to arrive, so colonists will not be able to call their families in real time. They are going to need strong teamwork and a lot of patience. Many experts think the first colonists will stay for at least three years.
